{{Short description|Maltese mathematician and hydrographer}}
[[File:Pagnini, Giovanni – Trattato della sfera ed introduzione alla navigazione per uso de' piloti, 1750 – BEIC 11342161.jpg|thumb|''Trattato della sfera'', title page]]

'''Giovanni Pagnini''' was an 18th-century Maltese mathematician and [[hydrographer]].<ref name=":0">{{cite book |title=Bibliografia militare italiana antica e moderna |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WwwUIGL4kwwC&pg=PA177 |last=D'Ayala |first=Mariano |publisher=Stamperia Reale |location=Turin |page=177 |language=it |date=1854}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Memorie della Accademia delle scienze dell'Istituto di Bologna|volume=4|location=Bologna|publisher=Tip. Gamberini e Parmeggiani|date=1882|page=500|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Q_goAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA500|language=it}}</ref>

He was a member of the [[Knights Hospitaller]].<ref name=":0" />

Born in [[Lucca]], Italy, Pagnini came to Malta known as the "Hydrographer of the Order" and the knowledge he brought was instrumental in the foundation of Malta's School of Navigation.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |url=https://mhs.mt/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/CrossCurrents_1989.pdf |title=Malta - a case study in international cross-currents |date=13–17 December 1989 |publisher=Malta University Publications |pages=130–133 |access-date=2025-03-19}}</ref>

Pagnini mainly expanded on theoretical mathematics, but his text ''Compasso di Proporzioni'' is focused on detailing new compass-like tools (ex: "''La Linea Aritmetica''", "''La Linea dei Piani[o] Linea Geometrica''", "''La Linea Cubica [o] Linea de Solidi''") for construction and navigation purposes.<ref name=":1" />
